title: What Employers Expect From You
summary: Learn the transferable behaviors employers commonly expect even when jobs require different technical skills.
objectives: Distinguish professional behavior from job-specific technical qualification.
Apply employer expectations to realistic workplace situations.

vocab.def: Being someone others can reasonably depend on to meet commitments and communicate when circumstances change.
Behavior that demonstrates responsibility, respect, judgment, and appropriate workplace conduct.
How well work meets the requirements or standards established for the task.
Information intended to help someone understand performance and improve future work.

sections.heading: Different jobs, shared expectations
sections.body: Jobs require different technical knowledge, credentials, tools, and responsibilities. However, many employers share expectations such as reliability, communication, honesty, respectful conduct, willingness to learn, teamwork, following procedures, and attention to quality.

sections.heading: Preparation is not qualification
sections.body: Learning professional behavior does not make someone qualified for every job. A healthcare worker, firefighter, electrician, technician, journalist, or aviation professional may need specific training, supervision, credentials, or authorization. Universal Career Readiness prepares you to function professionally while those separate requirements remain in place.

sections.heading: Employers need accurate communication
sections.body: Employers generally need workers to communicate accurately about progress, problems, delays, uncertainty, and support needs. Saying that something is complete when it is not can create greater risk than reporting the actual status.

sections.heading: Learning is part of the job
sections.body: New workers often need time to learn procedures, systems, terminology, and expectations. A strong learner listens, takes notes where appropriate, asks focused questions, applies feedback, and avoids repeating preventable mistakes.

practice.prompt: A new employee receives corrective feedback about a task. What response best demonstrates professionalism?
practice.answer: Listen, clarify anything that is unclear, make the required correction, and use the feedback to improve future work.

practice.prompt: A worker notices that a procedure is different from what they practiced in class. What should they do?
practice.answer: Follow the authorized workplace process and ask the appropriate person for clarification rather than assuming the classroom process overrides workplace requirements.

quiz.question: Which behavior is a transferable employer expectation across many industries?
options: Knowing every company procedure before the first day

lab.objective: Review workplace scenarios and identify which employer expectations are demonstrated or missing.

reflectionPrompt: Which employer expectation do you already demonstrate consistently, and which one would you most like to improve?
